attacks.claim: The embargo badge text is hard-coded to #ffffff on a background of var(--surface). In the default light theme --surface is #ffffff, so the badge text is invisible. Only the amber border remains visible.
attacks.evidence: .embargo { ... background: var(--surface); color: #ffffff; ... } with tokens.css setting --surface: #ffffff in :root

attacks.claim: The unpublish control is a span with an onClick handler and no role, tabIndex, or key handler. Keyboard-only editors cannot reach or activate it, which fails WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard, and the artifact states that some editors work keyboard-only.
The unpublish control contains only an icon marked aria-hidden and has no accessible name, so a screen reader announces nothing actionable for a destructive action (WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value).
attacks.evidence: <TrashIcon aria-hidden="true" /> with no aria-label or visually hidden text on the wrapping span

attacks.claim: handleUnpublish awaits onUnpublish with no try/catch and no error feedback. If the request fails after the confirm, the rejection is unhandled and the editor gets no signal that a story that must be pulled is still live.
attacks.evidence: if (ok) await onUnpublish(draft.id);  (no catch, no error state, no rollback or retry)

attacks.claim: The client sends draft.id to onUnpublish. The diff does not show a server-side authorization check for unpublish, so the control's safety depends on the backend, which this change does not establish.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: server-side authz for the unpublish action; diff only shows client handler

attacks.claim: No material privacy issue found under this lens.
No material sovereignty issue found under this lens.
No material scale issue found; each row computes one date comparison and renders one control.
No material cost issue found under this lens.

Unpublish returns the story to drafts, so it is reversible, but the artifact does not describe how an editor republishes from the queue. Restoring a story that was pulled in error means opening the draft, which the change is meant to avoid.
attacks.evidence: body: `"${draft.headline}" will be removed from the site and returned to drafts.`

attacks.claim: embargoed is computed during render against new Date(), so the badge does not update as the embargo lapses until the row re-renders.
attacks.evidence: const embargoed = draft.embargoUntil !== null && new Date(draft.embargoUntil) > new Date();

attacks.claim: The badge shows the lift time in newsroom time with no timezone label. Editors working from other zones may misread it.
The claim that unpublish currently takes four clicks and that editors open drafts only to check embargo status is not supported by any measurement or user data in the artifact.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any measurement or usage data behind "four clicks" and "keep opening drafts"

attacks.claim: No material ux-value issue found under this lens.
No material ux-efficiency issue found under this lens.
Embargo lift times are now shown on every queue row. The artifact does not state whether that visibility is permitted for all queue viewers under the newsroom's embargo rules.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: access rule for embargo visibility in the queue

attacks.claim: No material maintainability issue found under this lens.
